To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
calnexin is phosphorylated on its luminal and cytosolic domains, and that phosphorylation on its cytosolically exposed domain enhances the association of calnexins with membrane‐bound polysomes.

(1) calnexin is phosphorylated in vitro by ER‐associated kinases, (2) phosphorylation by these kinases leads to an increased association of calhexin with membrane‐associated ribosomes, (3) calnexin‐bound ERK‐1 is activated in vivo and (4) ERK‐1 activation by serum in cells leads to an increased ribosome‐associated phosphorylated calnexin.
calnexin is a target for phosphorylation by ER‐associated CK2 and ER‐associated ERK1, and that phosphorylation leads to an increased association of calnegxin with ribosomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a role for calnexin in the regulation of protein synthesis.
the role of the protein calnexin in the endoplasmic‐reticulum (ER).
the role of the phosphorylation of calnecin in the ER.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
calnexin is a multifunctional protein that can be regulated by a variety of mechanisms to perform its role in the ER.
calnexin is a substrate for ERK‐1 and CK2 in pancreatic microsomes.
phosphorylation of calnegin by CK2 and MEK‐1 enhances its association with ribosomes and thus with the translation apparatus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
phosphorylation of calhexin leads to increased ribosome association, and that the phosphorylation is a result of the activation of ERK‐2.
calnexin phosphorylation may be a mechanism to increase the rate of glycoprotein folding by enhancing the association of the calnexin–calreticulin chaperone system with ribosomes.
phosphorylation by CKII and ERK‐I enhances the association of calnexins with ribosomes and that this may be important in the control of glycoprotein folding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phosphorylation of cal- nexin by ER‐associated kinases can modulate the interaction of calnexin to ribosomes, and thus may play a role in regulating glycoprotein folding.
phosphorylation of calnaxin by CK2 and MEK1/ERK1 leads to a change in the subcellular distribution of calnexin, with an increase in association of calnexiin with ribosomes.
calnexin phosphorylation by CK‐2 and ERK1 leads to increased association with ribosomes and may facilitate the interaction between calnexin and the ribosomal translocon.
